arxiv-2012-11802.title: Structure-preserving, energy stable numerical schemes for a liquid thin film coarsening model
arxiv-2012-11802.creator: Juan Zhang, Cheng Wang, Steven M. Wise, Zhengru Zhang
arxiv-2012-11802.description: Abstract In this paper, two finite difference numerical schemes are proposed and analyzed for the droplet liquid film model, with a singular Leonard-Jones energy potential involved. Both first and second order accurate temporal algorithms are considered. In the first order scheme, the convex potential and the surface diffusion terms are implicitly, while the concave potential term is updated explicitly.

arxiv-2205-02017.title: so(2,1) algebra, local Fermi velocity, and position-dependent mass Dirac equation
arxiv-2205-02017.creator: Bijan Bagchi, Rahul Ghosh, Christiane Quesne
arxiv-2205-02017.description: Abstract We investigate the (1+1)-dimensional position-dependent mass Dirac equation within the confines of so(2,1) potential algebra by utilizing the character of a spatial varying Fermi velocity. We examine the combined effects of the two when the Dirac equation is equipped with an external pseudoscalar potential.

arxiv-2312-08212.title: LAMM: Label Alignment for Multi-Modal Prompt Learning Thanks: Corresponding Author.
arxiv-2312-08212.creator: Jingsheng Gao, Jiacheng Ruan, Suncheng Xiang, Zefang Yu
arxiv-2312-08212.description: Abstract With the success of pre-trained visual-language (VL) models such as CLIP in visual representation tasks, transferring pre-trained models to downstream tasks has become a crucial paradigm. Recently, the prompt tuning paradigm, which draws inspiration from natural language processing (NLP), has made significant progress in VL field.

arxiv-2412-06491.title: PPT: Pretraining with Pseudo-Labeled Trajectories for Motion Forecasting
arxiv-2412-06491.creator: Yihong Xu, Yuan Yin, Éloi Zablocki, Tuan-Hung Vu, Alexandre Boulch, Matthieu Cord
arxiv-2412-06491.description: Abstract Accurately predicting how agents move in dynamic scenes is essential for safe autonomous driving. State-of-the-art motion forecasting models rely on datasets with manually annotated or post-processed trajectories. However, building these datasets is costly, generally manual, hard to scale, and lacks reproducibility. They also introduce domain gaps that limit generalization across environments.

arxiv-2505-20788.title: Enhancing Wearable Tap Water Audio Detection through Subclass Annotation in the HD-Epic Dataset CCS: Human-centered computing Ubiquitous and mobile computing
arxiv-2505-20788.creator: Robin Burchard, Kristof Van Laerhoven
arxiv-2505-20788.description: Abstract . Wearable human activity recognition has been shown to benefit from the inclusion of acoustic data, as the sounds around a person often contain valuable context. However, due to privacy concerns, it is usually not ethically feasible to record and save microphone data from the device, since the audio could, for instance, also contain private conversations.

arxiv-2507-14529.title: Kernel Based Maximum Entropy Inverse Reinforcement Learning for Mean-field Games
arxiv-2507-14529.creator: Berkay Anahtarci, Can Deha Kariksiz, and Naci Saldi
arxiv-2507-14529.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Berkay Anahtarci, Can Deha Kariksiz, and Naci Saldi. We consider the maximum causal entropy inverse reinforcement learning problem for infinite-horizon stationary mean-field games, in which we model the unknown reward function within a reproducing kernel Hilbert space. This allows the inference of rich and potentially nonlinear reward structures directly from expert demonstrations, in contrast to most existing inverse reinforcement learning approaches for mean-field games that typically restrict the reward function to a linear combination of a fixed finite set of basis functions.

pmc-11436777.title: Modulation of αv integrins by lebecetin, a viper venom-derived molecule, in experimental neuroinflammation and demyelination models
pmc-11436777.creator: Nour-elhouda Neili, Zaineb AbdelKafi-Koubaa, Jed Jebali, Khouloud Kaidi, Ghada Sahraoui, Melika Ben Ahmed, Najet Srairi-Abid, Naziha Marrakchi, Raoudha Doghri, Ines ELBini
pmc-11436777.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Several neurodegenerative diseases, such as multiple sclerosis and Parkinson’s disease, are linked to alterations in myelin content or structure. Transmembrane receptors such as integrins could be involved in these alterations. In the present study, we investigated the role of αv-integrins in experimental models of neuroinflammation and demyelination with the use of lebecetin (LCT), a C-lectin protein purified from Macrovipera lebetina viper venom, as an αv-integrin modulator.

pmc-11594183.title: The Characterization and Stability of Powdered Oil Loaded with β-Carotene Prepared from a Sodium Caseinate–Carrageenan Complex: The Effect of Vacuum Freeze-Drying and Spray-Drying
pmc-11594183.creator: Yue Long, Juan Zhang, Delong Li, Yanpeng Zhang, Yang Cao, Wei Xu, Zhixiong Hu, Chun Hu
pmc-11594183.description: β-carotene (BC) has various biological activities, such as anticancer properties, contributing to the prevention of cardiovascular diseases, etc., while the poor solubility and low bioavailability limit its further development in the food industry. Therefore, how to effectively encapsulate this unstable substance has become a hot topic.

pmc-11626046.title: Bioactive peptides from food science to pharmaceutical industries: Their mechanism of action, potential role in cancer treatment and available resources
pmc-11626046.creator: Maryam Bidram, Mohamad Reza Ganjalikhany
pmc-11626046.description: Cancer is known as the main cause of mortality in the world, and every year, the rate of incidence and death due to cancer is increasing. Bioactive peptides are one of the novel therapeutic options that are considered a suitable alternative to toxic chemotherapy drugs because they limit side effects with their specific function.

pmc-11651884.title: The nature of ‘jaws’: a new predatory representative of Provora and the ultrastructure of nibbling protists
pmc-11651884.creator: Artem O. Belyaev, Sergey A. Karpov, Patrick J. Keeling, Denis V. Tikhonenkov
pmc-11651884.description: The recently discovered Provora supergroup has primarily been examined to determine their phylogenomic position in the eukaryotic tree. Their morphology is more poorly studied, and here we focus on their cellular organization and how it compares with that of other supergroups.

pmc-11689027.title: NIGROSTRIATAL DOPAMINE AND PHYSICAL PERFORMANCE FATIGABILITY IN COMMUNITY-DWELLING OLDER ADULTS
pmc-11689027.creator: Caterina Rosano, Emma Gay, Paul Coen, Andrea Rosso, Anne Newman, Stephen Kritchevsky, Nancy Glynn
pmc-11689027.description: Increasing nigrostriatal dopaminergic signaling can ameliorate performance fatigability in healthy young adults, but its role in community-dwelling older adults is not known. We hypothesized higher nigrostriatal dopaminergic integrity would be associated with lower performance fatigability, independent of other factors that impact physical performance fatigability, including cardiorespiratory fitness and muscle energetics.

pmc-11690252.title: SOCIAL INVISIBILITY OF ELDER ABUSE IN FAMILIES: A PHENOMENON IN PHILIPPINE SOCIETY
pmc-11690252.creator: Carmelina Oyales, Victoria Apuan
pmc-11690252.description: In a country where the prevailing culture is to give respect and care for the older persons, elder abuse is an interesting phenomenon. The study focuses on elder abuse and the different forms of abuse occurring in Filipino communities. The authors undertook a qualitative study composed of individual interviews of ten victims of elderly abuse.

pmc-12973420.title: Extracts of Black Glutinous Rice Influenced Memory Impairment and Anxiety-Like Behavior associated with Kidney Stones in Rats
pmc-12973420.creator: Parinyaporn Nuurai, Nantapong Pea-arun, Nattawee Kuntawee, Racha Muengsuwan, Jirasuda Nakeim, Sri-arun Iamjan
pmc-12973420.description: This study investigated the effects of “Luem Pua” black glutinous rice extract on behavior and neuronal integrity by assessing memory impairment, anxiety-like behavior, histology, as well as expression of brain-derived neurotrophic factor (Bdnf) and caspase-3 (Casp3) genes in a rat model of kidney stone disease.

pmc-13458469.title: Managing Mental Health Crises in Indonesian Universities: A Reflexive Thematic Analysis of Psychologists' Experiences
pmc-13458469.creator: Aisha Sekar Lazuardini Rachmanie, Yesica Grahita Rumanti Mahambara, Restu Tri Handoyo, Subandi
pmc-13458469.description: IntroductionMental health issues have become a major concern in universities worldwide, including in Indonesia. Various mental health challenges experienced by students can trigger crises, such as urges to self-harm or even suicidal ideation. Such crises require immediate intervention. However, access to mental health emergency services remains limited and lacks standardized guidelines.

pmc-13470315.title: Accurate prediction of gain- and loss-of-function missense variants in GABAA receptors
pmc-13470315.creator: Christian M. Boßelmann, Sebastian Ortiz, Rebekka Dahl, Vivian W.Y. Liao, Serene El-Kamand, Susan X.N. Lin, Anthony Sze Hon Kan, Tobias Brünger, Dennis Lal, Holger Lerche, Jules Kreuer, Nico Pfeifer, Mary Chebib, Nathan L. Absalom, Philip K. Ahring, Rikke S. Møller
pmc-13470315.description: SummaryBackgroundMissense variants in genes encoding GABAA receptors are involved in the pathophysiology of common and rare epilepsies. Variant effects on channel biophysical function are associated with key clinical characteristics and treatment response. Predicting variant effects is therefore key to improving care for individuals with GABAA receptor-related disorders.

uslaw-usc-t18-s3497.title: 18 U.S.C. § 3497 — Account as evidence of embezzlement
uslaw-usc-t18-s3497.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t18-s3497.description: United States Code, Title 18 (Crimes And Criminal Procedure); Part II (Criminal Procedure); Chapter 223 (Witnesses And Evidence). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Upon the trial of any indictment against any person for embezzling public money it shall be sufficient evidence, prima facie, for the purpose of showing a balance against such person, to produce a transcript from the books and proceedings.
